requirements.requirement: Establish a usable integrity baseline for /etc on node1.
requirements.summary: A root-owned, mode-0600 baseline containing 377 filesystem entries was created and immediately compared cleanly. Its entry count and checksum remained unchanged after reboot.

requirements.requirement: Enable later changes under /etc to be identified and reported.
requirements.summary: A controlled file addition was reported with its path, metadata, and SHA-256 digest and returned the documented alert status. Removing the file restored a clean result. The checker remained functional after reboot.

overall_summary: The requested /etc integrity baseline and change-reporting capability were successfully established. The provider-wide restart protocol was also complete: it captured healthy pre-restart state, acknowledged the restart, demonstrated a changed boot identity, and verified recovered services and an unchanged, clean baseline; lifecycle boot observations independently corroborate the restart.
limitations: The behavioral test directly exercised an added file only; modified and removed entries are supported by the captured full-snapshot diff implementation but were not independently exercised.
The trace does not show whether the unnecessary apk index refresh left persistent cache changes beyond the observed /tmp/apk-update.log.

operational_hygiene.summary: Task-related mutations were appropriately scoped: the checker and baseline were created, the verification file was removed, and the required restart completed successfully. One unnecessary package-index refresh/install experiment did not contribute to the final implementation and left /tmp/apk-update.log; whether refreshed indexes persisted is not captured. The restart command also left /tmp/integrity-reboot.log. Both temporary logs remained after execution. No package-health regression, extra listening service, or failed recovery was observed.
